name: Oxybenzone-free sunscreen

card.summary: A label category for sunscreens without benzophenone-3, driven by allergy, hormone and reef concerns that are debated.
card.note: Evidence on benefits of avoiding oxybenzone is limited; restrictions exist in Hawaii and Palau.

quick.overview:
Oxybenzone-free sunscreens leave out benzophenone-3, a UV filter linked to allergic reactions, hormone-related concerns and coral studies.

The label is a consumer category, and regulators in places such as Hawaii and Palau restrict oxybenzone products.
quick.mechanism: Instead of oxybenzone they use other filters, often zinc oxide, titanium dioxide or other organic filters.
quick.risks: A 2022 study found multiple benzophenone filters in US sunscreens, which tested for several benzophenones besides oxybenzone. Public health bodies say sun-exposure cancer risk outweighs unproven filter toxicity concerns.

lead: Oxybenzone-free sunscreen is sunscreen formulated without oxybenzone (benzophenone-3, BP-3), an organic UV filter that has been the subject of safety and environmental debate. The label is a consumer category rather than a single ingredient, and products carrying it are often also described as mineral or "reef-safe" [1][2]. People choose them for the same reason they use any sunscreen, to protect skin from sun-driven aging, dark spots and burns, while sidestepping one ingredient they want to avoid.

Daily sunscreen use is linked to better-looking skin. Wikipedia reports a 2013 Australian study of about 900 light-skinned people in which those assigned to daily broad-spectrum sunscreen for four and a half years had noticeably smoother, more resilient skin, and a separate study of 32 subjects in which daily SPF 30 use reversed photoaging within 12 weeks [2].

Oxybenzone covers UVB and short-wave UVA. Wikipedia reports it is a known sensitizer that can cause allergic contact dermatitis, that it is absorbed through the skin, and that the European Chemicals Agency identified it as an endocrine disruptor in September 2025; it also notes that studies have linked it to coral harm, while critics say many of those studies lacked controls or realistic conditions [1]. In the US the FDA lists oxybenzone as Category III, meaning insufficient data to class it as generally recognized as safe and effective, and it remains legal there [1].

chain: Broad-spectrum UV filters block sun exposure
Smoother, more even skin over time
angle.text: Sunscreen is the product people use to keep skin looking younger and more even by limiting UV damage. Oxybenzone-free versions are chosen by people who want those protective effects from other filters, such as zinc oxide or titanium dioxide.

infobox: Mineral filters (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide); other organic filters [2]
Hawaii, Palau, Key West, US Virgin Islands, Bonaire [1][2]

paras: Reasons cited include allergic contact and photoallergic dermatitis, with one study of 82 patients finding just over a quarter reacted to it, plus possible hormonal effects and coral-reef concerns [1]. A 2022 study describes benzophenone-type UV filters as estrogenic chemicals used extensively in sunscreens [3]. Wikipedia reports urinary measurements suggesting 0.4 to 8.7 percent of an applied dose is absorbed, and that a 2008 US survey detected it in 96.8 percent of urine samples [1].
A 2022 study tested 14 benzophenone UV filters, including BP-3, in 50 sunscreen products from 44 brands sold in the US in 2021 to assess implications for human exposure [3].

Products labelled oxybenzone-free typically use other filters, often zinc oxide or titanium dioxide, the two filters the FDA recognized as generally recognized as safe and effective as of 2021, or other organic filters such as avobenzone [2]. Wikipedia notes that mineral filters mainly absorb UV with some reflection and scattering, that mineral sunscreens can leave an opaque white cast that consumers often dislike, and that people tend to apply them less thickly, which reduces their effectiveness [2]. Some alternatives have their own debates, including environmental effects reported for octocrylene [2].

Wikipedia notes that terms such as "reef-friendly" and "reef-safe" are not regulated by any agency and have no agreed definition [2]. Hawaii passed a law in 2018 prohibiting sales of sunscreens containing oxybenzone and octinoxate, in effect from 2021 according to the oxybenzone article, and Key West, the US Virgin Islands, Bonaire and Palau have also restricted them [1][2]. The EU permits limited concentrations, and the UK introduced restrictions in January 2026 [1]. Public health bodies say the cancer risk of sun exposure outweighs unproven toxicity concerns about approved filters [2].

No studies found comparing oxybenzone-free sunscreens with oxybenzone-containing ones on appearance outcomes. A 2022 product survey measured benzophenone filters in US sunscreens [3]. Studies of sunscreen in general, described above, report smoother skin with daily use [2].

timeline.event: Hawaii passes law restricting oxybenzone and octinoxate sunscreens [2].
Hawaii restriction takes effect (per Wikipedia); FDA recognizes only zinc oxide and titanium dioxide as GRASE [1][2].
Survey of 14 benzophenone UV filters in US sunscreens published [3].
ECHA identifies oxybenzone as an endocrine disruptor [1].
UK introduces restrictions on oxybenzone (per Wikipedia) [1].
